title: Visual Composition
outcome: By the end, I can check object counts and spatial relations as separate visual requirements.
scenario: A fictional Study Buddy requests a science-poster layout, then audits a supplied drawing description.
given: Brief: exactly two labelled bottles left of one beaker; one arrow from bottles toward beaker.
Supplied drawing description: two labelled bottles are right of a beaker; an arrow points from beaker toward bottles.

steps.label: Count objects
steps.detail: Two bottles and one beaker satisfy the count requirement.

steps.label: Check position
steps.detail: Bottles on the right fail the required left-of relation.

steps.label: Check direction
steps.detail: Arrow from beaker to bottles reverses the required flow.

steps.label: Repair brief
steps.detail: Specify bottles-left, beaker-right, arrow left-to-right; verify the revised output.

explanation: Having every requested object is not the same as conveying the requested relationship. Position and arrow direction can change a scientific explanation while object counts remain correct. Audit the provided description honestly: no actual image was supplied, so this evaluation concerns its stated layout rather than a claimed visual inspection.

counterfactual.change: Move bottles left of the beaker but keep the arrow pointing from beaker toward bottles.
counterfactual.prediction: Position now passes; arrow direction still fails.
counterfactual.reason: Changing object placement does not automatically reverse an arrow’s semantic source and destination.

student_task: Which checks pass after that single change, and what still needs repair?
teacher_answer: Counts and left-of position pass. Direction still fails: arrow must originate at bottles and point toward beaker.
project_evidence: Create Study Buddy diagram rubrics covering counts, readable labels, containment, order and meaningful arrow direction.
limits: A compliant layout does not by itself verify the chemistry or procedure represented; content needs source checking.
review_note: Individually designed fictional worked case, distinct from the reserved assessment. Toy model simplifications, arithmetic and source authority reviewed explicitly.
